title: Epochal Sparkline: Guardian Mode for low-power accessible time-series
creator: Ava Ramirez
description: Problem: High-density time-series panels in dashboards consume CPU/GPU and cause jank on low-power devices; tooltips and legend hover interactions are inaccessible to keyboard and screen-reader users. Goal: Design a "guardian mode" rendering profile for sparklines and compact charts that reduces paint cost, preserves semantic data access for ATs, and exposes a single-keyboard-friendly summary interaction. Also align visual tokens and color contrast with the design system token set so runtime can swap between energy/performance profiles.
background: Usage analytics show >30% of dashboard views come from devices with low Chrome power_profile (phones, tablets, small laptops). Existing compact charts render per-point hover layers and expensive axis tick calculations even when not focused. Accessibility tests flagged missing aria-live summaries and no keyboard affordance to step through series. Engineering has an experimental runtime flag (render_mode=guardian) but needs design definitions and acceptance criteria to implement consistently across Console components.
goals: Define visual and interaction spec for Guardian Mode (reduced layers, static axes, precomputed decimation)
Provide keyboard-first interactions with single summary toggle and accessible ARIA announcements
Update design tokens for sparkline color ramps and stroke widths to map to energy-friendly runtime profiles
Deliver assets and annotations for engineers: low-fidelity comps, final tokens, acceptance tests, and perf budget targets
constraints: Must be implementable with existing Canvas and SVG fallbacks in runtime
Cannot require additional network roundtrips or server-side decimation for first iteration
Must support dynamic theming (light/dark) and color tokens available in tokens v3
Latency SLO for dashboard render should not increase; per-chart CPU should decrease on low-power devices
acceptance_criteria: Guardian Mode toggle exists on compact chart component and defaults to off; when on, charts render with no interactive hover layers by default
Keyboard users can focus a compact chart and press Space to open a single accessible summary panel that exposes latest value, delta, and CTA (drill-in)
Screen readers receive aria-live updates when the summary panel appears; the underlying canvas remains reachable via an offscreen accessible table if requested
Design tokens for sparkline_stroke, sparkline_fill_opacity, axis_text_small map to new token names and are documented in tokens/docs/charting.md
Perf regression tests show >=30% CPU reduction on simulated low-power profile compared to baseline for 1,000-point series
Engineering accepts the spec and implements a runtime flag render_mode: guardian with documented fallback to full rendering
deliverables: Token mapping doc and token names for engineering
Keyboard and screen reader interaction flow and aria pattern examples
Performance targets and recommended decimation heuristics
Design handoff package: SVG/PNG comps, redlines, and a short demo recording
out_of_scope: Full redesign of large lens charts
Custom analytics instrumentation beyond existing dashboard metrics
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Guardian Mode may hide important anomalies — Mitigation: add configurable thresholds and highlight outliers even in guardian mode
Risk: Screen reader users lose fine-grained point access — Mitigation: include a simple table export and an optional traverse-by-index keyboard affordance
Risk: Color token mismatch with older releases — Mitigation: provide a compatibility map and fallback tokens
implementation_notes: Prefer precomputed downsampling (LTTB or fixed-interval min/max) at component mount to avoid per-frame decimation
Limit canvas repaint to <2 times during initial paint when guardian mode enabled
Replace hover tooltips with single summary overlay; keep legend interactions intact for expanded charts
Use CSR-friendly ARIA pattern: role='region' + aria-labelledby for the summary panel and aria-live='polite' for value updates
